version.changelog:
extract-memories 2.0.0 — Major overhaul with topic-based memory files

- 记忆文件结构彻底重构：对话记忆按 topic 类型分别写入 memory/topics/ 目录下独立文件，不再按日期分文件
- 新增 MEMORY.md 索引文件，纯做 topic 文件指针管理，不含记忆正文
- 记忆分类精简为 user/feedback/project/reference 四种类型，清晰区分用途和存储结构
- 每条记忆文件带标准 frontmatter（name、description、type）
- 严格定义不可持久化内容（如代码结构、git 历史、临时任务等），避免保存冗余/不适用信息
- 新增详细样例与输出模板，确保主会话反馈结构统一

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 2.0.0

The extract-memories skill is a utility designed to summarize conversation highlights and store them in a local 'memory/' directory. The instructions in SKILL.md define a structured process for categorizing information (user, feedback, project, reference) and explicitly forbid saving sensitive or redundant technical data like code structures or Git history. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection were found.

llm.summary: The skill's requested actions (reading the recent conversation and writing topic files under memory/) match its stated purpose of extracting and persisting memories; nothing indicates covert behavior or unrelated privilege requests.

dimensions.detail: Name/description say 'extract memories to topic files' and the instructions only ask to read conversation context and write/append files under memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md. Required capabilities described in SKILL.md (FileRead, FileWrite/FileEdit) are appropriate and proportional to that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Overall instructions stay within the stated purpose and explicitly ban reading source repos, git history, or saving code structure. Two areas to note: (1) the skill says it will use the '最近 N 条对话' but N is unspecified, giving the agent discretion that could expand data collected; (2) it prefers updating existing topic files (which implies reading memory/topics/ to find matches). Both of these are reasonable for the feature but are somewhat open-ended and worth confirming with the skill author or operator policy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with no install spec or third-party downloads. No code files to execute and no binaries required, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. The only resources it needs are file read/write permissions for the agent's memory directory and optional ability to spawn sessions, which are proportional to its stated function.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). However the skill is designed to run automatically at conversation end (autonomous invocation is platform-default), so it will persist conversation-derived content to disk unless the user disables or revokes it. The optional sessions_spawn (forking a child agent) is a more powerful capability and should be considered before granting; it is reasonable for advanced workflows but increases blast radius if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: read recent conversation text and append curated 'memory' topic files under memory/topics/ and update MEMORY.md. Before installing or enabling automatic runs, consider: (1) privacy — the skill will persist conversation content to disk, so avoid saving sensitive secrets unless you want them stored; (2) confirm how many recent messages ('N') it will inspect and whether that scope is acceptable; (3) decide whether you want automatic background extraction after every conversation or prefer manual trigger (/extract-memories); (4) be cautious about enabling sessions_spawn (child agent forks) unless you trust the skill and need that behavior. If any of these are unclear, ask the skill author for exact defaults (N, conflict-resolution rules) or restrict the skill to manual invocation and review the created files periodically.
